claim_scope_statement: Bounded schedule exploration under the bounds below is systematic concurrency testing, never proof (assurance/concurrency/plan.json claim ceiling). Native-thread stress samples schedules without coverage accounting and cannot stand in for the systematic result, nor the systematic result for native-thread evidence.
recorded_at_provenance: captured from `date -u` at write time, immediately after the pre-landing review (session 01a04960) fix run whose printed counters this document transcribes; blob ids and artifact digests computed from the tree being committed
revision_note: supersedes the 3df6371 revision after a PRE-LANDING review (session 01a04960-1698-7302-85c3-c1d467a50937) returned 5 blocking findings, every one of which was REPRODUCED BY EXECUTION before it was fixed. (1) Post-shutdown automatic responses could commit new writes and emit MULTIPLE drop reports: a congested event queue refuses the latched EOF non-fatally, so a Ping delivered on a post-shutdown poll found the core still Open and its automatic pong committed a frame the ended transport could never carry. FIXED by gating the injection on !shutdown_latched. The companion claim that max_dropped_frames_in_one_report == 1 is STRUCTURAL was false and is corrected: under the default policy a report legitimately carries two frames (frames=2,bytes=12), now pinned. (2) Real adapter teardown bypassed DriverInput::Shutdown on hard socket errors, mid-handshake EOF, rejected input and both poll-budget exits; FIXED by routing every such exit through io_loop::end_transport_service. (3) The native receiver-drop race test was vacuous - deleting the whole receiver-drop arm left it reporting ok - and now REQUIRES a typed post-drop observation with receiver_dropped asserted == 1. (4) The adapter's dropped-write accounting had no consumer: deleting both increments left `make -C rust gates` at exit 0 with ac1-gates 8/8. Three loopback tests over real sockets now assert the returned ConnectionReport. (5) The PASS evidence was internally inconsistent - a stale 53,247/26,673 classification, 1024 misattributed to the ConnectionConfig default (the real default is 64; 1024 is the harness's MAX_ACTIONS_UNREACHED), and a round-2 'polarity' seed declaring mutation=none. All three are corrected, and a genuinely rerunnable round-2 control is committed at fuzz-seeds/us017/controls/fatal-halt-write-drop-accounting.seed. SWEEP COUNTERS ARE UNCHANGED: the exploration runs AutoResponsePolicy::Disabled, so the driver fix cannot move it - re-executed and read identical (79,920 schedules, 18,755 trace digests, 56,777/23,143 closed/halted, 37,813 reports / 134,430 bytes / 4,172 partial-front, 79,920 receiver-drop refusals, fatal sweep 56,189 / 198,037 with per-budget 7,572/23,072/13,985/11,560). The seven pinned minimized artifacts and both regression seeds are byte-identical and were not refrozen. Prior revision notes (session 01a0464f round 2, and BLOCKING-1/2 of session 01a04626 with the stale preregistered_plan.sha256 correction) remain in force.

adapter_model: the interpreter drives the public driver boundary exactly as the real adapter does: a surfaced DriverOutput::Failure HALTS the run at that instant (ws-testee io_loop maps it to LoopOutcome::ProtocolFailure and stops), so no schedule action, drain poll, or quiescence poll follows a Failure; Terminal-after-Failure is impossible by construction and additionally asserted

execution.replay_determinism: every schedule executed twice with FULL structured-trace equality: every poll record compares the input (kind + byte length), the complete typed input disposition (rejection details included), the complete command disposition (command payloads and typed rejection failures included), the complete owned output (semantic-event contents, typed failure values, byte-exact write suffixes), and the lifecycle state; the enumeration itself is re-run and compared; trace digests hash the full structured records plus the committed wire log
execution.terminal_disposition_exclusivity: asserted per run AND in aggregate: terminals total 56777 == closed_terminal_runs (exactly one each), surfaced failures total 23143 == failure_halted_runs (exactly one each, the halting failure); 56777 + 23143 == 79920

counters.reconciliation: clean-terminal runs reconcile EXACTLY per run (accepted == applied + rejected + terminal_rejected); halted runs assert at-most-once disposition of accepted commands, with commands still queued at the halt belonging to the embedding adapter's teardown (aggregate disposed 210047 of 222723 accepted; the 12676 remainder were queued at halt boundaries and never double-disposed)

execution.outcome: PASS - zero invariant violations across all 79920 schedules in the main sweep and across all 79920 schedules at each of the 4 fatal-termination action budgets
execution.new_disposition_coverage: US-017 AC2 story-review dispositions are REACHED by the sweeps, not only by unit fixtures. Receiver-drop: all 79,920 schedules end with a deterministic post-run EPILOGUE that drops the sole owner and probes the producer seam once, and every one refuses with CommandRefusalReason::ReceiverDropped rather than accepting. SCOPE (pre-landing review finding 3, session 01a04960): that counter equals the schedule count because the epilogue runs exactly once per schedule. It exercises the typed refusal from every END STATE the sweep reaches; it explores no receiver-drop RACE, since the drop and the send are sequenced on one thread. The racing evidence is the native-thread test ws-core/tests/concurrency_boundary.rs::a_producer_racing_the_owner_drop_never_blocks_and_never_reports_a_stale_accept. Dropped writes, CLEAN route: 37,813 of the 79,920 schedules shut down with a committed write pending and every one surfaced exactly one typed report whose frames/bytes/partial_front matched the boundary's independent count of what the ended transport owed (134,430 undelivered bytes, 4,172 with a partially written front frame). Dropped writes, FATAL route (round 2): the same schedule space re-swept under action budgets 0/1/2/3 exercises fatal termination with abandoned committed writes 56,189 times (198,037 undelivered bytes; per budget 7,572 / 23,072 / 13,985 / 11,560), and the same owed-vs-reported equality holds on every one

fatal_termination_sweep.why: the main sweep's action budget is the harness constant MAX_ACTIONS_UNREACHED (1024, chosen by rust/ws-driver/tests/schedule_exploration.rs so the budget cannot bind), far above the 12-action alphabet, so no schedule there can terminate fatally with a pending dropped-write report. That unreachability is exactly what let the round-2 defect hide. CORRECTION (pre-landing review finding 5): this field previously called 1024 the ConnectionConfig default; it is not. The real ConnectionConfig default for max_actions is 64 (rust/ws-core/src/config.rs, LimitField::MaxActions), and 1024 is the exploration harness's own deliberately unreachable budget.
fatal_termination_sweep.method: the SAME exhaustive enumeration (79,920 schedules, identical alphabet, bounds, and capacities) re-executed under tightened max_actions budgets so ActionLimitExceeded ends runs fatally while committed writes are outstanding; each schedule executed twice for replay equality, all invariants asserted, and the boundary's owed-vs-reported equality applied to halted runs too
fatal_termination_sweep.exclusivity: asserted per run at every budget: halted runs have exactly one surfaced failure and zero terminals, non-halted runs converge with exactly one terminal and zero failures, and halted + closed == 79920 at each budget
fatal_termination_sweep.receiver_drop: 79,920 typed receiver-drop refusals at every budget: the disposition holds under fatal termination too
fatal_termination_sweep.harness_polarity_read: the sweep was run against the PRE-FIX driver and FAILED as required: "budget 1: schedule enqueue-text-a,enqueue-binary-a,enqueue-ping-b,enqueue-close-b,inbound-ping,inbound-close,transport-eof,write-partial,wake,shutdown,write-all,write-all violated [UnreportedWriteDrop]". That read is a WORKING-SESSION observation and is not rerunnable from the committed tree, because a pin against the shipped driver cannot replay a pre-fix one. The RERUNNABLE round-2 polarity evidence is rust/ws-driver/fuzz-seeds/us017/controls/fatal-halt-write-drop-accounting.seed, whose declared mutation (drop-writes-dropped-report) is parsed and executed on the fatal-halt route by schedule_exploration.rs::round_two_fatal_halt_accounting_control_replays_both_polarities: faulted it must record UnreportedWriteDrop on a halted run, clean it must surface exactly one report before the halting failure. Re-exempting halted runs from check_write_drop_accounting was executed and read: the faulted run reported write_drop_reports=0 dropped_frames=0 with violations [] - the control goes red, which is what makes it a control.

terminal_disposition_model: every full schedule reaches EXACTLY ONE typed terminal disposition, mirroring the real adapter: the clean Terminal from the absorbing Closed state (56777 runs, exactly one Terminal each, zero surfaced failures), or the halt at the first surfaced fatal Failure (23143 runs, exactly one surfaced failure each, zero Terminals) - the poisoned core retains its final state per the oracle's partial-execution semantics and the adapter stops there; both classes fully quiesce, clean-terminal runs reconcile every accepted command exactly once. The typed dropped-write disposition is NOT a third terminal: it precedes the Terminal (or the halting Failure) in the same run and is scored on BOTH routes. CORRECTION (pre-landing review finding 5, session 01a04960): this field previously retained the pre-round-2 53247/26673 split and said drops were scored only on non-halted runs. Both were stale - the round-2 fix moved the split to 56777/23143 and extended the boundary's owed-vs-reported equality to halted runs, which is the exemption that had hidden the defect.

defects_found_and_fixed.red_evidence: both regression tests were executed against the pre-fix driver (fix stashed) and their failures were read; both pass with the fix restored

defects_found_and_fixed.finding_verbatim: AC2 lacks a typed receiver-drop outcome; sends can return accepted after the sole owner has been dropped.
defects_found_and_fixed.description: ws_core::CommandSender::try_send returned Ok(()) after the sole owner (CommandQueue, held by ConnectionDriver) was dropped, admitting the command into a bounded queue that no owner would ever drain. The prior US-017 closure pinned that acceptance as CORRECT (driver_contract.rs: expect("capacity admits one command even with the owner gone")), so the gap was actively locked in by a test.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: CommandChannel carries a receiver_dropped flag set by Drop for CommandQueue while it HOLDS the queue lock; try_send reads it inside the same lock, so the flag and the push are decided in one critical section and no send can be accepted past a receiver that is going away. The refusal uses the incumbent refusal vocabulary (new CommandRefusalReason::ReceiverDropped), not a parallel mechanism, and is terminal for the channel.
defects_found_and_fixed.red_evidence: read on the pre-fix driver: `a send after the sole owner is dropped must never report accepted: ()` - the `()` is the Ok(()) the send actually returned

defects_found_and_fixed.finding_verbatim: AC2 silently abandons committed pending writes on adapter shutdown instead of reporting the required typed dropped-write disposition.
defects_found_and_fixed.description: ConnectionDriver::poll(DriverInput::Shutdown) discarded the offered write and drained the core's remaining wire writes with `while self.core.next_write().is_some() {}` - correct to abort, but nothing was reported, so a producer that had already seen CommandDisposition::Applied was left believing bytes it will never see were sent
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: abort_pending_writes accounts every abandoned committed write into a DroppedWrites{frames,bytes,partial_front} report surfaced as DriverOutput::WritesDropped ahead of DriverOutput::Terminal; next_output re-sweeps on every post-shutdown poll so a write appearing after shutdown would be aborted and reported too rather than offered to a dead transport
defects_found_and_fixed.red_evidence: read on the pre-fix driver: `the abandoned committed suffix is reported, not silently dropped: ["event", "event", "event", "event", "terminal"]` / left: Some("event") right: Some("writes-dropped:frames=1,bytes=3,partial_front=true")

defects_found_and_fixed.finding_verbatim: A pending `WritesDropped` disposition is suppressed by a fatal `Failure`, after which the adapter halts, leaving a reachable committed write silently unreported.
defects_found_and_fixed.description: ConnectionDriver::finish_poll returns a supplied fatal TypedProtocolFailure WITHOUT calling next_output, so a DroppedWrites report set moments earlier by the Shutdown arm was never surfaced. The latched EOF is applied inside that same shutdown poll, and it fails fatally with ActionLimitExceeded once the action budget is spent, so the whole observable output of the run became a single Failure and the committed frame vanished. A faithful adapter halts at its first Failure, so anything queued behind it is unreachable by construction.
defects_found_and_fixed.ac_reading: AC2 lists adapter shutdown in the same typed-behaviour clause as every other terminal disposition and carves out no exception for fatal termination; 'cannot leak' is unconditional, so the report is owed on the fatal route exactly as on the clean one.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: has_pending_output now counts an undelivered DroppedWrites report alongside an offered write, so the driver applies NO input while one is outstanding. A fatal failure can only be produced by APPLYING an input, so none can exist to suppress the report. Structural, not an ordering rule: the report is surfaced strictly before any failure can be generated. Schedules with nothing committed pending are bit-for-bit unaffected, because the report is only set when frames > 0.

defects_found_and_fixed.description: ConnectionDriver::next_output sweeps abandoned writes before draining events, but the automatic-pong injection at the event-drain site did not check shutdown_latched. handle_eof needs MAX_EVENT_SLOTS_PER_INPUT (4) free event slots, so a congested event queue refuses the latched EOF non-fatally and the core is still Open when a queued Ping is delivered on a post-shutdown poll. The injected pong then commits a frame the ended transport can never carry, and the next poll's sweep surfaces it as a SECOND WritesDropped report.
defects_found_and_fixed.reproduction_read: swept 756 candidate configurations (event_queue_capacity 4..24 x 1..4 queued pings x 0..8 pre-drains) at the public driver boundary under the DEFAULT policy; capacity=6 with one queued ping and no pre-drain read: SHUTDOWN => writes-dropped:frames=1,bytes=3 / post1 => Event(Ping{data:[0]}) / post2 => writes-dropped:frames=1,bytes=3. With the fix, zero configurations in the same swept space produce more than one report.
defects_found_and_fixed.fix: next_output injects the automatic reply only while !shutdown_latched, the same stance the Shutdown arm already took for PARKED replies (pending_auto_pongs.clear()). No wire behaviour before shutdown moves, and the exploration sweep counters are byte-identical because it runs AutoResponsePolicy::Disabled.

max_dropped_frames_in_one_report is 1 across all 79920 schedules of THIS sweep, which runs under the explicit AutoResponsePolicy::Disabled configuration. CORRECTION (pre-landing review finding 1, session 01a04960): the previous text called that value structural, and it is not. Under the DEFAULT AutoResponsePolicy::PongInboundPing an automatic pong is injected while a semantic event is being RETURNED, so it never passes through the offered-write gate; it sits in the core's write queue while the next poll applies a producer command on top of it, and the shutdown that follows reports frames=2,bytes=12. That was reproduced by execution before this correction was written and is now pinned by driver_contract.rs::a_shutdown_report_accounts_for_every_committed_frame_not_just_the_offered_one. The plural accumulation in abort_pending_writes is therefore an EXERCISED path under the shipped default, and only the report COUNT (one per run) is a bounded property; the frame count is not.

assurance/concurrency/plan.json is preregistered and was NOT edited by this revision, so its action vocabulary still names neither a dropped-write outcome under action.shutdown (SHUTDOWN_IDEMPOTENT, LATE_CONNECTION_GOING_AWAY, DRAIN_WINDOW_BOUNDED) nor any receiver-drop action at all. The two AC2 dispositions added here are therefore evidenced by the exploration and the unit suites, not by the preregistered action model

the fatal-termination sweep reaches fatal termination via ActionLimitExceeded (a tightened max_actions budget), which is one fatal family, not all of them. It is the family reachable from the existing 12-action alphabet without changing the alphabet or the pinned corpus; other fatal refusals are covered only insofar as they share the same finish_poll path, which they do by construction

a fatal Failure halt with NO shutdown ever polled leaves committed writes with the driver rather than abandoned by it, so no dropped-write report is owed there; the ws-testee io_loop deliberately does not pump Shutdown on its protocol-failure path, because a run that surfaced a fatal Failure stops at that instant by contract and never polls again. That is the pre-existing adapter-teardown stance the suite already takes for commands queued at a halt, and it is the ONLY remaining no-shutdown exit. NARROWED (pre-landing review finding 2, session 01a04960): the stance used to cover far more than that. drive_until_open returned on a hard handshake write error, on a hard read error, on mid-handshake EOF, on a rejected input, and on both budget exits WITHOUT pumping Shutdown, and drive_connection could exhaust its poll budget the same way - so a BrokenPipe handshake write or a max_polls=1 run silently abandoned its committed frames. Every one of those exits now calls io_loop::end_transport_service before the caller drops the driver, pinned by loopback.rs::a_hard_handshake_write_error_shuts_down_and_reports_the_committed_request and loopback.rs::an_exhausted_poll_budget_shuts_down_and_reports_the_abandoned_committed_writes.
